survivors.title: kindle_post OCF re-zip stamps every non-mimetype member with wall-clock time → Kindle catalog assets are NOT byte-reproducible
survivors.evidence: Both re-zip sites pass a bare string filename (not a ZipInfo) to writestr: `zout.writestr(name, data[name])` (lines 201 and 662). Python's zipfile, when given a str arcname rather than a ZipInfo, constructs `ZipInfo(filename=name, date_time=time.localtime(time.time())[:6])` — i.e. it stamps the member's central-directory date_time with the CURRENT WALL-CLOCK time. So `make_kindle_safe` (the M4 Send-to-Kindle catalog post-process) and `apply_kindle_m4b` produce a different central directory on every run, even from byte-identical input. No `date_time` is pinned anywhere in the module (grep for `date_time`/`1980`/`_ZIP_EPOCH` returns only `_DOC_SUFFIXES`). This directly contradicts the module docstring: `"-> OCF re-zip (mimetype first + stored)"` described as a "deterministic post-process" (lines 1, 26, 29-32). The sibling packagers DO pin it: build_epub.build sets `zi.date_time = (1980,1,1,0,0,0)` for every entry (build_epub.py:149/156) and swap_epub_cover.swap_cover sets `zi.date_time = _ZIP_EPOCH` (swap_epub_cover.py:33/64). The dedicated guard tests/test_epub_zip_determinism.py asserts `zi.date_time == ZIP_EPOCH` for every entry of build_epub output and documents this exact bug class — but kindle_post was written without applying the same fix, and tests/test_kindle_post.py only checks mimetype-first/stored + content transforms (lines 169-190), never two-build byte equality nor date_time, so the regression escapes. The flagship byte-stability gate (tests/test_byte_stability_gate.py) builds only everywhere-base editions (`_EDITIONS = [ethiopian-tewahedo, catholic-study, evangelical-reformed]`) and never invokes the kindle post-process, so it cannot catch this either. The mimetype member alone is safe (it is written via an explicit `ZipInfo("mimetype")`, whose constructor default date_time is the 1980 epoch). Impact: the shipped Kindle column assets (build_format_matrix.py `_apply_kindle_post` → make_kindle_safe, run LAST on the bytes) and their SHA256SUMS are not reproducible across the required v1.0.0 re-cut (SESSION_STATE: "release assets ... re-cut at tag"), violating the project's core byte-stability invariant for that format.
survivors.fix: Pin every member's date_time (and, to fully match the sibling packagers, external_attr) at both re-zip sites. Define `_ZIP_EPOCH = (1980, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)` at module scope and replace the bare-string writestr in the loops with an explicit ZipInfo, mirroring swap_epub_cover.swap_cover: for each non-mimetype `name`, build `zi = zipfile.ZipInfo(name); zi.date_time = _ZIP_EPOCH; zi.external_attr = 0o644 << 16; zi.compress_type = zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED; zout.writestr(zi, data[name], compresslevel=9)`. Also set `date_time`/`external_attr` on the explicit mimetype ZipInfo for parity (lines 197 and 658). Apply identically in both make_kindle_safe (195-201) and apply_kindle_m4b (657-662). Then extend tests/test_kindle_post.py with a determinism case (two make_kindle_safe runs of the same input → identical bytes, and every infolist().date_time == _ZIP_EPOCH), matching test_epub_zip_determinism.py, so this class can never regress again.
survivors.verifierFix:
At module scope in scripts/core/kindle_post.py add `_ZIP_EPOCH = (1980, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)`. At BOTH re-zip loops (make_kindle_safe lines 195-201 and apply_kindle_m4b lines 657-662) replace the bare-string writestr with an explicit ZipInfo, mirroring swap_epub_cover.swap_cover:

    mz = zipfile.ZipInfo("mimetype"); mz.date_time = _ZIP_EPOCH; mz.external_attr = 0o644 << 16; mz.compress_type = zipfile.ZIP_STORED
    zout.writestr(mz, data["mimetype"])
    for name in order:
        if name == "mimetype":
            continue
        zi = zipfile.ZipInfo(name); zi.date_time = _ZIP_EPOCH; zi.external_attr = 0o644 << 16; zi.compress_type = zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED
        zout.writestr(zi, data[name], compresslevel=9)

The date_time + external_attr pin is the load-bearing part (it is what makes the central directory reproducible). compresslevel=9 is OPTIONAL — include it to match the sibling packagers (build_epub / swap_epub_cover, which feed these inputs at level 9), or omit it to keep the byte change minimal; either way the output becomes deterministic. Apply identically at both sites. Then add a determinism case to tests/test_kindle_post.py mirroring tests/test_epub_zip_determinism.py: run make_kindle_safe twice on the same synthetic input and assert byte-identical output, and assert every infolist().date_time == _ZIP_EPOCH, so the class cannot regress. This change is additive, leaves the 9 KJV editions byte-stable, and touches no marathon-core file.

survivors.title: Kindle post-process re-zip is non-reproducible (drops the M14 date_time / external_attr pin) — 2 sibling sites
survivors.evidence:
make_kindle_safe re-zips every non-mimetype member with a bare-string name:
```
with zipfile.ZipFile(dst_epub, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zout:
    zout.writestr(zipfile.ZipInfo("mimetype"), data["mimetype"], compress_type=zipfile.ZIP_STORED)
    for name in order:
        if name == "mimetype":
            continue
        zout.writestr(name, data[name])
```
Passing a *string* name to ZipInfo-less writestr makes zipfile stamp `date_time = time.localtime(time.time())[:6]` into every member header, so each run yields a different central directory (different bytes, different SHA-256). It also drops the `external_attr = 0o644 << 16` perms bit. This contradicts build_epub.build, which deliberately pins both for the EPUB packager: `mz.date_time = (1980, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)` / `zi.external_attr = 0o644 << 16` with the comment "so the central directory is reproducible across checkouts ... (M14)". apply_kindle_m4b (line 657-662) has the identical pattern. I checked both re-zip sites in kindle_post.py; build_standalone.py is off-limits and build_epub.py already pins correctly, so these are the only two defective sites.
survivors.fix: In both make_kindle_safe and apply_kindle_m4b, build a pinned ZipInfo per member instead of passing a bare string: `zi = zipfile.ZipInfo(name); zi.date_time = (1980, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0); zi.external_attr = 0o644 << 16; zi.compress_type = zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED; zout.writestr(zi, data[name])` (and set the mimetype ZipInfo's external_attr to match). This restores M14 reproducibility so the released Kindle artifact's SHA256 is stable across re-cuts. A small unit test that re-runs make_kindle_safe twice and asserts byte-identical output pins it.
survivors.verifierFix:
In BOTH make_kindle_safe (kindle_post.py ~195-201) and apply_kindle_m4b (~657-662), replace the bare-string writestr loop with a pinned ZipInfo per member, mirroring scripts/swap_epub_cover.py:60-71 and scripts/build_epub.py:153-159:

  mz = zipfile.ZipInfo("mimetype")
  mz.date_time = (1980, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
  mz.compress_type = zipfile.ZIP_STORED
  mz.external_attr = 0o644 << 16
  zout.writestr(mz, data["mimetype"])
  for name in order:
      if name == "mimetype":
          continue
      zi = zipfile.ZipInfo(name)
      zi.date_time = (1980, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
      zi.external_attr = 0o644 << 16

(The compresslevel=9 matches build_epub/swap_epub_cover; the prior bare writestr silently produced level-6 bytes — a separate consistency drift.) Add a unit test that runs make_kindle_safe (and apply_kindle_m4b) twice on the same input and asserts byte-identical output, mirroring tests/test_epub_zip_determinism.py. This restores M14 reproducibility so the Kindle artifact's SHA-256 is stable across re-cuts and brings the two sites into line with the project's established re-zip convention.

survivors.title: No maximum-piece-size gate: round-9 kepub regressed to an 882 KB piece — past the 881 KB size EREADERS records as having broken Kobo rendering
survivors.evidence: verify_kr2_build's gate 1 ("piece geometry") computes `sizes.append(len(t))` for every `index_split_*` piece and only PRINTS them — `print(f"sizes: min {min(sizes):,}  max {max(sizes):,} ...")` (lines 723-726) — but never asserts a ceiling; no `fails.append` is keyed on size. The shipped round-9 ethiopian-tewahedo kepub measures **Max piece size 882 KB** (`docs/superpowers/notes/2026-06-18-kobo-round9-tap-list.md:61`, "Maintainer measurements (this artifact)"). EREADERS.md:93-94 records the design state as "round-2: 881 KB pieces broke rendering; now max ~405 KB / mean ~233 KB", and the LANE_HANDOFF log credits the splitter fix with "killed the 700-880 KB over-cap pieces → max 405 KB". The default target is `FILE_SPLIT_TARGET_DEFAULT = 400_000` (build_edition.py:4444). Both splitters allow a single atom to stand alone over-cap with no hard ceiling: scripture `split_html_document` greedy-packs "a lone over-weight atom stands alone" (build_edition.py:4801-4821) and glossary `split_study_glossary_document` cuts only at book/entry boundaries — "K-R10: never pack two canon books into one glossary piece" (build_edition.py:5011-5021), so a single heavily-studied book's glossary can exceed target unbounded (CHANGELOG.md:494 already records "largest piece ~720 KB"; round-9 grew it to 882 KB after the +72 restored comm/word notes). The only size-related test merely checks a glossary piece is smaller than the un-split monolith — `assert max(len(t.encode('utf-8')) for _,t in pieces) < len(text.encode('utf-8'))` (tests/test_file_split.py:1003) — which is trivially true for any split. So nothing (gate or test) catches an over-ceiling piece, and the artifact shipped at exactly the historical break size.
survivors.fix: Add a hard piece-size gate to dev/verify_kr2_build.py gate 1: after collecting `sizes`, `fails.append` when `max(sizes)` exceeds a renderer-safe ceiling (e.g. 450_000-500_000 bytes raw, with a separate higher allowance only for kindle-target artifacts whose KFX paginates internally — detect via the `yhwh:target-reader` OPF stamp already read at line 128). In the builder, give the glossary splitter the same within-book sub-cut the scripture splitter has: when one `study-book-head` group exceeds target, additionally cut between `study-glossary-cat`/`study-glossary-entry` blocks (the atoms already exist via `_study_glossary_chunk_atoms`) so no single book strands an 882 KB piece — preserving the K-R10 'book head leads its piece' rule but capping size. Re-measure round-9's worst book to confirm it falls under the new ceiling, then add a test asserting `max piece bytes <= ceiling` over the real catalog fixture, not just < monolith.
survivors.verifierFix: Optional hygiene only (not a hard gate): add a non-failing WARN to dev/verify_kr2_build.py gate 1 that surfaces oversize pieces by BYTES, not codepoints — e.g. after the loop, compute `byte_sizes = [len(zf.read(n)) for n in pieces]` and `print(f"WARN (1-size): {n} = {b:,} bytes" )` for any piece whose UTF-8 byte length exceeds a comfort threshold (~500_000). Keep it a WARN, never fails.append, so the byte-stable 9 KJV editions and the device-PASS round-9/13 Ethiopian artifact are not regressed by a new FAIL on already-accepted ~700-932 KB pieces. Do NOT add the proposed builder sub-cut: the glossary chunker already cuts within a book at study-glossary-entry boundaries (build_edition.py:4971-4978). If a real device paging-jank failure is ever evidenced at these sizes (none is on record — round-13 PASS), THEN lower FILE_SPLIT_TARGET_DEFAULT or tune split_study_glossary_document per the existing round-9 P2 deferral (platform-kobo.md:159) — that is editorial/QA-gated, not an audit-mandated hard gate.

survivors.title: Build inject->filter->zip path: CONFIRM-OPTIMAL (no safe speedup that preserves byte-stability)
survivors.evidence: Re-evaluated the per-edition pipeline against the optimization mandate. Each build_one: shutil.copytree(EPUB_DIR, tmp) (~23 MB), runs in-memory-consolidated filter/transform passes (Round-9 Opt#2 already batches HTML reads into pre_badge_texts/repair_texts single load+write cycles), then subprocess build_epub.py which zips at compresslevel 9. main() already parallelizes --all on `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=min(len(targets), 5))` backed by the content-addressable build_cache (compute_cache_key hashes the whole epub_working tree + corpus + pipeline scripts) plus is_output_current mtime check. The three candidate optimizations all fail the byte-stability obligation or are already declined: (a) compresslevel 9->6 is explicitly DECLINED on the merits (1-3% size growth); (b) a shared pre-filtered base cannot be shared across editions because every edition diverges at the FIRST pass (filter_html drops different kinds, then per-edition renumber/badge/canon-splice/file-split mutate the tree differently) — there is no common post-filter prefix to cache; (c) more parallel workers would OOM the 16 GB box (round-7 finding). The base IS already cached unchanged across editions via the epub_working tree hash; cache hits skip the entire pipeline and serve the stored EPUB. The only residual cost is genuinely-parallel independent per-edition zip work, which is the irreducible floor.
survivors.fix: No change. The pipeline is optimal under the constraints (byte-identical 9 KJV editions, 16 GB RAM, quality-over-speed compresslevel). Byte-stability proof obligation is already satisfied: any future change must regenerate all 9 editions and `git diff` to prove byte-identical output (RULES byte-compat invariant), which no proposed speedup here can meet.

BUT this is NOT a current defect, and the finder concedes as much ("if that ordering ever inverts, or a new aside emitter is added"). The build is presently CORRECT: (a) baked vnote asides already carry separators from bake-time (generate_verse_popups.py:56 calls add_vnote_preview_separators); (b) the build-pass re-application is guarded by negative-lookaheads (?!<span class="vn-sep">) (core/vnote_separators.py:10-11) so it idempotently adds separators only to the translation-swap output, whose vnote-source-label/vnote-text paragraphs the regexes DO match. So swapped paragraphs are correctly re-covered today. Blast radius is bounded to the CSS-blind Kobo eInk preview only — .vn-sep is display:none everywhere CSS applies (build_edition.py:2577), so there is zero shipped-render corruption and the 9 KJV editions stay byte-stable. Coverage already exists at the function/unit level (test_marker_style.py:519-577) AND at the standalone artifact level (test_build_standalone.py:159-164 asserts all vnote-text blocks in the built EPUB carry vn-sep). This finding is a defense-in-depth gate request for a hypothetical future regression (ordering inversion / new emitter), not a shipped bug. Per the round-10 down-calibration rule (bounded blast radius, no output corruption, KJV byte-stable), it is info-tier hardening at most.

The proposed fix is SAFE and additive (a read-only artifact gate; no engine/schema change; does not touch the marathon core; cannot affect byte-stability), and it does close a documented sweep item, so it has modest value as a regression backstop. But severity as a *defect* is none — refuted.

dropped.title: Gate 4g/4n label oversized vnote asides 'un-probed class' and WARN-only, although the vnote class is device-PROVEN to decline
dropped.reason: I read the cited gates in dev/verify_kr2_build.py (4g lines 193-209, 4n lines 320-340) and the device-QA notes the finding rests on. The code claims are accurate: gate 4g/4n FAIL oversized class="verse-notes" asides and only WARN oversized class="vnote" asides with an "un-probed class" message, and those warns (printed at main() lines 699-700/716-717) do not enter the `fails` list so they do not affect the exit code. BUT the finding's load-bearing premise — that round-4 device QA PROVED the vnote (translation) class declines — is a misread. The two surfaces are distinct: (1) translation popups = `<aside class="vnote" id="vnote-{b}-{c}-{v}">` (build_edition.py:797,822 — id prefix `vnote-`, no `s`); (2) merged study asides = `<aside class="verse-notes" id="vnotes-{code}-{ch}-{v}-s1">` (build_edition.py:3866 — id prefix `vnotes-`, with `s`). The device-declined ids cited by the finder (`vnotes-gen-1-26`, `vnotes-gen-1-1`) carry the `vnotes-` prefix, i.e. they are verse-notes(study)-class asides — the class the gate ALREADY FAILs. The finder conflated the `vnotes-` id prefix with the `vnote` class. The round-5 device QA proves the OPPOSITE for the actual vnote class: round5-device-qa.md line 27 "translation popups all popped", and line 176 "vnote-1ki-12-24 at 6,937 — the un-probed translation-popup class, round-5 taps all popped." The gate's own comment (verify_kr2_build.py:172-175) documents this exact rationale (round-5 taps showed them all popping → honest WARN under no-reassert-ratified-bar). This also matches the round's settled-items #14 (vnote-1ki-12-24 = fix-arc-in-flight WARN) and #15 (adjacent vnote prefix = WARN not FAIL). I checked all four vnote-vs-verse-notes branch sites (4g lines 205-208, 4n lines 336-339); both correctly mirror the same intended convention. The proposed fix (flip vnote→FAIL) is unsafe: it would convert a device-proven-popping class into build-blocking false failures with no device evidence. The only residual merit is a minor wording nit ("un-probed" is mildly stale since round-5 did tap several vnote popups and they popped — "device-proven-popping / honest WARN" would read better), which is info-level polish, not a medium defect, and does not justify the FAIL-flip.
